events.title: Joseph tells Pharaoh his family has come
events.narrative_summary: Joseph goes in and tells Pharaoh that his father and brothers, with their flocks and herds, have come from Canaan and are in Goshen.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. In 46:31 Joseph says he will go up and tell Pharaoh, so it follows his instructions at Goshen (46:31–34). The journey from Goshen to the court is not stated; `urim travel loc.goshen loc.egypt --mode chariot` gives about 112 km by road, 12 km/h, 9.4 h moving, elapsed about 1 day. So offset 1 day from the end of the instructions, margin 1 day for the unstated departure and route. Duration: a short report.

events.title: Five brothers tell Pharaoh they are shepherds
events.narrative_summary: Joseph presents five of his brothers to Pharaoh. They say they are shepherds, as their fathers were, and ask to dwell in Goshen because the famine has left no pasture in Canaan.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the report in 47:1; the text marks no gap, so it starts at the end of that event. Duration about half an hour for the interview; margin one day.

events.title: Pharaoh tells Joseph to settle his family in Goshen
events.narrative_summary: Pharaoh tells Joseph the land of Egypt is open to him, that his father and brothers may live in the best of it, in Goshen, and that capable men among them may oversee Pharaoh's livestock.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Pharaoh answers in the same audience, so it starts when the brothers' request ends. Duration minutes; margin an hour.

events.title: Jacob stands before Pharaoh and blesses him
events.narrative_summary: Joseph brings Jacob before Pharaoh and Jacob blesses him. Asked his age, Jacob says he has sojourned a hundred and thirty years, few and evil, and blesses Pharaoh again as he leaves.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Joseph brings Jacob in after Pharaoh's grant (47:5–6); no gap is stated, so it follows the grant, margin one day. Jacob's age of 130 matches anchor.jacob_birth + 130 years, about 1876 BCE, which is the date of the arrival; I do not anchor twice, see the reviewer note.

events.title: Joseph settles his family in the land of Rameses
events.narrative_summary: Joseph settles his father and brothers and gives them a possession in the best of the land, the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Carrying out Pharaoh's order (47:6). The text gives no delay; I put it one day after the audience, a week's duration, margin a week, for moving a household of seventy to the Goshen/Rameses region (about 90 km from Egypt's centre on the packet's figures).

events.title: Joseph feeds his father's household with bread
events.narrative_summary: Joseph provides bread for his father, his brothers and all his father's household, according to their families' needs.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: A standing provision through the famine, from the settlement on. The famine had begun about two years before Jacob's arrival (45:6) and lasts seven years, so about five years remain: duration five years, margin one year.

events.title: Joseph gathers all the money of Egypt and Canaan
events.narrative_summary: With no bread anywhere and Egypt and Canaan faint from the famine, Joseph collects all the money paid for grain and brings it into Pharaoh's house.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No date given. The money paid for grain (41:56–57) is gathered from the start of the famine until it fails (47:15). Ramban on 47:18: Joseph gathered it over five years, since the money lasted until the sixth year, when 47:17 (Sforno) has the people bring cattle. So it starts with the famine (evt.gen_41.famine_begins) and runs about 4.7 years, to the start of the cattle exchange (about three years after the settlement); margin a month on the start.

events.title: The Egyptians trade their livestock to Joseph for bread
events.narrative_summary: When money fails, the Egyptians come to Joseph asking for bread, and he takes their horses, flocks, herds and donkeys in exchange, feeding them for that year.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Sforno on 47:17: this is the sixth year of the famine. Jacob came in about year 2 (45:6), so year 6 begins about three to four years after the settlement: offset 3 years, margin 1 year; duration the one year the text names ("for that year").

events.title: The Egyptians offer their land and themselves to Pharaoh
events.narrative_summary: The Egyptians say their money and cattle are gone and ask Joseph to buy them and their land for bread and seed. Joseph buys all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: First beat of the year, anchored on the parent's start; the sale takes about a month, margin a month.

events.title: In the next year the Egyptians sell their land and themselves
events.narrative_summary: The year after the cattle exchange, the Egyptians come to Joseph with nothing left but their bodies and land. Joseph buys the land for Pharaoh, moves the people to the cities, and sets a fifth of the harvest as Pharaoh's share.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: "When that year was ended... the second year" (47:18): Rashi says the second year of the famine, but Sforno, reading it as the second year after the money ran out, the seventh year of the famine. I follow Sforno, which fits a seven-year famine. It starts when the cattle year ends, margin a month; duration one year.
events.ancient_year_marker: When that year was ended... the second year

events.title: Joseph moves the people to the cities
events.narrative_summary: Joseph moves the people to cities from one end of Egypt's borders to the other.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the purchase; no delay stated. Duration a month for a nationwide movement, margin a month.

events.title: Joseph gives the people seed and sets a fifth for Pharaoh
events.narrative_summary: The priests' land is not bought, since they live on Pharaoh's allowance. Joseph gives the people seed and decrees that a fifth of the harvest belongs to Pharaoh. The people say he has saved their lives, and it becomes law to this day.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Joseph speaks "this day" (47:23): "I have bought you this day", so the seed and the decree come on the day of the purchase, at the end of the sale (47:18–20); the relocation of 47:21 runs alongside, not before. Anchored on the end of the sale, no delay; duration a day; margin a month. The aside on the priests (47:22) and the law of 47:26 are covered here.

events.title: Israel lives in Goshen, grows and multiplies for seventeen years
events.narrative_summary: Israel settles in Goshen, acquires property and multiplies greatly. Jacob lives seventeen years in Egypt, reaching 147.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Seventeen years stated (47:28), counted from Jacob's arrival (Joseph's meeting with him in Goshen, 46:29). Cross-check: anchor.jacob_birth + 147 years lands at the end of this span. Margin a month for the arrival date.
events.ancient_year_marker: Seventeen years in the land of Egypt

events.title: Jacob makes Joseph swear to bury him in Canaan
events.narrative_summary: As his death nears, Israel calls Joseph, has him put his hand under his thigh, and asks not to be buried in Egypt but with his fathers. Joseph swears, and Israel bows on the head of the bed.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: "The days of Israel drew near that he must die" (47:29), at the end of the seventeen years, before 147. Offset 16.5 years from the start of his stay with a six-month margin, since the text does not say how close to death. Rashi notes that "drew near" is said of those who did not reach their fathers' age.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Joseph's coaching of his brothers to say they are shepherds (46:31–34) leads Pharaoh, on hearing it (47:3–6), to place them in Goshen.
God's word at Beersheba, "I will there make of thee a great nation" (46:3), is borne out when Israel grows and multiplies exceedingly (47:27).
With money and cattle gone, only bodies and land are left, so the people offer them (47:18–19).
After buying the land, Joseph gives seed and fixes the fifth (47:23–26).
Once Joseph has drained all the money, the people, whose money has failed, must offer livestock for bread (47:15–17).
Joseph settles the family in Rameses "as Pharaoh had commanded" (47:11).

entities.etymology_meaning: Not a name; the Hebrew simply says 'five men' from among his brothers.
entities.summary_bio: Five of Joseph's brothers whom he picks to stand before Pharaoh. The text does not name them. They state their trade as shepherds and ask to settle in Goshen.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew kohanim, 'priests'; here the Egyptian temple priesthood.
entities.summary_bio: The priestly class of Egypt, who live on a fixed allowance from Pharaoh. They are the one group whose land Joseph does not buy for the crown during the famine.

entities.etymology_meaning: Egyptian in origin, probably 'Ra has fashioned him'; the name of the later Ramesside royal city.
entities.summary_bio: The district of Egypt where Joseph settles his father and brothers by Pharaoh's command, 'the best of the land'. The text uses it for the same region as Goshen; later it names a store-city built by Israel's enslaved descendants.

components.evidence_explanation: Gen 47:19 they offer to be servants of Pharaoh; 47:23 Joseph says 'I have bought you today'; 47:25 they accept.
Gen 47:29 'the days of Israel drew near to die'.

components.label_value: A possession in the land of Rameses
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 47:11 Joseph gives them a possession in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses.
Gen 47:27 'they were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly'.

components.label_value: Sworn to bury Israel in Canaan
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 47:29–31 Israel asks him to carry him out of Egypt and bury him with his fathers, and Joseph swears.

components.label_value: Owns all of it except the priests' land
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 47:20 'the land became Pharaoh's'; 47:22 and 47:26 exempt the priests' land.
Gen 47:22 the priests have an allowance from Pharaoh and so do not sell their land.

systems.name: Blessing of a ruler
systems.ancient_near_east_context: A visitor of standing could greet or take leave of a king with a blessing. A patriarch blessing a king reverses the usual rank, since the blesser is taken to be the greater party.
rules_and_mechanics: Spoken by an elder or holy man over a ruler.
Given on entering and on leaving the audience.
Presumes the giver speaks with God's favour.

systems.name: Purchase of land for the crown
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In Egypt and the wider Near East the crown and temples held much of the land, and cultivators worked it for a share. A famine-time transfer of private holdings to the king, with the farmers staying on as tenants, fits the royal and temple estates known from Egyptian records.
rules_and_mechanics: Owners hand their field to the crown in exchange for food and seed.
The sellers stay on the land as tenants of the king.
Land held by a privileged class may be exempted.

systems.name: Royal tax of one fifth
systems.ancient_near_east_context: A fixed share of the harvest owed to the crown is a standard form of royal tenancy rent and taxation in the Near East. The text presents this fifth as a standing law 'to this day'.
rules_and_mechanics: A fifth of each harvest goes to the king.
The other four parts remain with the farmers for seed and food.
Set by statute (choq) and not renegotiated each year.
Priests' land is outside the rule.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Israel asks not to be buried in Egypt but to lie with his fathers in their burial place; Joseph agrees to do as he said.
system_instances.significance_note: Shows that Israel still counts Canaan, not Egypt, as home.

system_instances.outcome_summary: When the money is gone the Egyptians bring horses, flocks, herds and donkeys, and Joseph gives them bread for a year.
system_instances.significance_note: The second stage: with no silver left, the people hand over their animals to be fed.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Joseph gives the people seed and sets by statute that a fifth of the harvest goes to Pharaoh; the priests' land stays theirs.
system_instances.significance_note: Turns the emergency purchase into a lasting arrangement, and shows Joseph as an administrator who saves life while strengthening the crown.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Joseph collects all the silver of Egypt and Canaan paid for grain and brings it to Pharaoh's house.
system_instances.significance_note: The first stage of the famine sales, which move the wealth of two lands to the crown.

system_instances.outcome_summary: In the second year the Egyptians offer themselves and their land for bread and seed, and Joseph buys all the land for Pharaoh.
system_instances.significance_note: The third stage completes the move of Egypt's land and people to Pharaoh through Joseph's management.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Israel has Joseph put his hand under his thigh and swear to carry him out of Egypt; Joseph swears and Israel bows on the bed's head.
system_instances.significance_note: Binds Joseph to return the family's body to Canaan and keeps the hope of the promised land alive while Israel lives in Egypt.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob blesses Pharaoh when he is brought in and again when he leaves, and answers Pharaoh's question about his age.
system_instances.significance_note: The patriarch carrying Abraham's promise blesses the king of Egypt, echoing the promise that nations are blessed through his line.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Pharaoh tells Joseph to settle his father and brothers in the best of the land, in Goshen, and to put capable men over his livestock.
system_instances.significance_note: The king's invitation turns a famine refuge into a settlement and gives Israel a home in Egypt.

edges.description: The brothers say they are shepherds who came to sojourn because of the famine, and ask to live in Goshen.
The Egyptians, with no money left, ask Joseph for bread so they do not die.
The Egyptians offer themselves and their land to be Pharaoh's servants in return for bread and seed.
Israel makes Joseph swear to bury him in his fathers' grave in Canaan.
Jacob blesses Pharaoh when Joseph brings him in.
Israel, near death, calls his son Joseph to him.
Joseph buys all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh.
Joseph gives bread in exchange for the people's livestock and feeds them for that year.
Joseph supplies his father's whole household with bread according to the number of their little ones.
Joseph gathers up all the silver paid for grain in Egypt and Canaan and brings it to Pharaoh's house.
Joseph tells Pharaoh that his father and brothers have arrived from Canaan and are in Goshen.
Joseph moves the people into the cities from one end of Egypt to the other.
Joseph takes five of his brothers and sets them before Pharaoh.
Joseph sets as a statute that the Egyptians give a fifth of the harvest to Pharaoh.
Joseph settles his father and brothers in the land of Rameses and gives them a possession, as Pharaoh commanded.
Joseph swears to his father that he will do as he asked.
Pharaoh tells Joseph to settle his family in Goshen, the best of the land, and to appoint capable brothers over his livestock.
Pharaoh gives the priests a regular allowance, so they have no need to sell their land.
Pharaoh asks the brothers what their occupation is.
Pharaoh asks Jacob how many years he has lived.
